title: hx-trigger: Event Filters, Debounce (delay), and Throttle Modifiers

progressiveExplaining.eli5: If you are searching in an encyclopedia, you don't want to run to the library after every single letter you type. `hx-trigger` lets you say: 'wait until I stop typing for half a second (`delay:500ms`) and only search if the word actually changed (`changed`)'.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `hx-trigger` customizes which events fire an HTMX request and applies rate-limiting modifiers. Common syntax: `hx-trigger="keyup changed delay:500ms"` (debounced search), `hx-trigger="click throttle:1s"` (prevents double-clicks), `hx-trigger="load"` (fires on page load), `hx-trigger="revealed"` (fires when element scrolls into view). You can also use event filters: `hx-trigger="click[ctrlKey]"`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `hx-trigger` provides declarative event stream conditioning directly in HTML attributes. It supports event filters (JavaScript boolean expressions evaluated against the event object `[event.target.value.length > 3]`), polling schedules (`every 2s`), external trigger listeners (`from:body`, `from:document`), and custom event triggers (`hx-trigger="itemAdded from:body"`). This replaces complex RxJS `debounceTime`/`distinctUntilChanged` operator chains.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: HTMX parses the `hx-trigger` attribute string into a trigger specification AST. When an event fires, HTMX evaluates the bracketed condition `[eval(condition)]`. For `delay:X`, it resets an active `setTimeout` timer (debounce). For `throttle:X`, it drops events arriving before the cooldown timer expires. For `changed`, it compares `element.value` against its previously cached value.

codeComparison.title: RxJS/Lodash Debounce Implementation vs hx-trigger Modifiers
codeComparison.summary: Debouncing live search manually requires external libraries and state; `hx-trigger` configures debounce in one line.

legacyOrBad.label: Manual JS Debounce Search
legacyOrBad.snippet: let timer; input.onkeyup = () => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(fetchResults, 500); }; // ❌ Verbose

modernOrGood.label: Declarative HTMX Debounced Search
modernOrGood.snippet: <input hx-get="/search" hx-trigger="keyup changed delay:500ms" hx-target="#results" /> // ✅ NEW

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `delay:500ms` and `throttle:500ms` in `hx-trigger`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Tests your understanding of debounce vs throttle algorithms in UI events.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `delay:500ms` is a **debounce**: it waits until 500ms have elapsed *since the last event* before firing the request (ideal for typing in search boxes). `throttle:500ms` is a **rate limiter**: it fires the request immediately on first trigger, and then ignores all subsequent triggers for the next 500ms (ideal for preventing double-clicking on submit buttons).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Using `throttle` instead of `delay` on a search input will cause intermediate requests to fire mid-word while typing.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you trigger an HTMX request based on a custom event emitted from another element?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of cross-component event coordination in HTMX.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Use the `from:` modifier: `hx-trigger="cartUpdated from:body"`. When any element in the application dispatches `document.body.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('cartUpdated'))`, the targeted element catches the event and executes its `hx-get` request.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If you omit `from:body`, the element will only listen for events dispatched directly to itself or bubbling through its own children.
